subject: Money
title: Cost-Push Inflation
description: A fast breakdown of Cost-Push Inflation for builders.

hook.text: In 1973, Arab nations cut oil exports. Gas prices quadrupled. Everything that moved cost more overnight.

buildup.text: Cost-push inflation starts with rising input costs: oil, wages, raw materials. Producers pass costs to consumers.

discovery.text: Oil touches everything: shipping, plastics, farming, heating. When oil spikes, the entire economy inflates.

twist.text: Cost-push inflation is harder to fix. Raising interest rates kills demand but doesn't lower oil prices.

climax.text: The 1970s saw both supply shocks and loose money. The combination—stagflation—was the worst of both worlds.

punchline.text: When costs rise, everyone feels it.
